regulation.summary: The Public Charge Point Regulations 2023 set no limit on how often data users may request the data. Regulation 10(5) requires the data to be available free of charge without terms on its use. DfT's guidance allows terms covering the means of access, which is where operators' rate limits come from.

quotes.text: terms and conditions covering the means of access to the data and API(s) are permissible
quotes.source: DfT, Public Charge Point Regulations 2023 guidance

vat_rule.summary: OCPI 2.2.1 prices exclude VAT, and each price can give the VAT rate that applies to it. Where every price in a tariff gives a rate, this project adds it and shows the price including VAT. A price with no rate is read by OCPI as having no VAT, but VAT on public charging in the UK is at the standard rate of 20%, so such a price is likely to be lower than what a driver pays.
vat_rule.observed: In the daily run of 22 October 2026, 10 of the 12 operators fetched gave a VAT rate on their prices, and char.gy and Clenergy EV gave none. char.gy's own pricing page gives each of its prices 20% higher than its feed does. Clenergy EV's website gives no charging prices, but 120 of the 126 prices per kWh in its feed come to a whole penny once 20% is added. The details are in each operator's findings above.
vat_rule.decision: The repository owner decided on 22 October 2026 that prices on the map should all include VAT, so they can be compared. For each operator listed here, VAT at the rate shown is added to every price that gives no rate, and the price says this project added it. A price with no rate from any other operator is shown as published and marked "VAT not stated". The tariffs themselves are published unchanged.
vat_rule.in_price: A feed can state a VAT rate on prices that seem to include VAT already: BrightGreen's display price equals the price with no VAT added, and some feeds give every price in whole pence as published, which adding the rate would not. Adding the rate would then show a price higher than the operator seems to charge. On 23 and 29 October 2026 the repository owner decided that for each operator listed here, the VAT its feed states is read as already in its prices: each price is shown as published, including VAT, and says so. This is inferred from the figures, not stated by the operators.

private_rule.summary: The repository owner decided on 11 October 2026 that chargers marked as not for public use are hidden on the map unless a visitor ticks "Show chargers marked private or restricted" in the filters. OCPI 2.2.1 has no field that says a location is private, and no feed read so far marks one in any other field, so a location is marked only when the operator's own name for it contains one of these phrases, as whole words in any mix of capitals:
phrases: "private use", "private access" or "private only", as in "Private Use Only"
"private" at the end of the name or in brackets, as in "Site - PRIVATE"
"staff only", "fleet only", "employees only", "residents only", "tenants only", "members only" or "permit holders only", with or without "use" before "only"
private_rule.taxis: Separately, where the owner has decided so for an operator (see Sources above), a location where the operator marks every charge point for taxis only is hidden in the same way, and each such charge point is labelled "Taxis only".
private_rule.not_counted: Words that often name a place rather than a rule, such as "Fleet" in Fleetwood Road, "Depot", "Residential", "Visitor Centre" or "Blue Badge holders only", are not counted. A marked location is published unchanged: its details say which words were found, and the feed health page lists every location marked in the latest run.

findings.handling: char.gy was left out of that run. The gap between requests was raised from 2 to 6 seconds the same day, and the next run (37856014933, the same evening) fetched every page and published 5,948 locations.

findings.summary: A one-off full fetch made on 2026-10-09 to check coordinates, from a network other than GitHub's and with the 4 second gap, was answered HTTP 403 for offset 2700, after 54 pages. The daily run of the same day fetched every page.
findings.handling: The check stopped there and was not retried. All of char.gy's mapped locations were checked from the published map instead. The one location left off the map in that day's run (listed in that run's manifest) could not be looked at and needs checking in a later run. The daily run's gap is unchanged, since the owner's rule is about refusals in the daily run.

findings.summary: In a daily run started by hand on 2026-10-09 at 17:51 UTC from a GitHub Actions runner, with the 4 second gap, the locations feed answered HTTP 403 for offset 2800, after 56 pages. Across the three refusals so far (offsets 2900, 2700 and 2800, with gaps of about 2.8 and 4 seconds, from two networks) the feed refused after 54 to 58 requests each time, while the run with a 6 second gap fetched all of about 120 pages. findings.handling: char.gy was left out of that run's map. The gap went back to 6 seconds, as recorded under rate_limit. Since ADR 0018, a refusal part-way through a run is followed by a wait of 5 minutes and a wider gap before the page is asked for again, at most twice, and if the fetch still fails the map keeps showing the last good copy with its date.

findings.summary: Tesla's developer page says the Tesla Roaming Portal, through which it offers an OCPI connection, is currently available on a pilot and invitation basis only. A connection needs a Tesla Account and a request that Tesla reviews. Neither the public page nor the signed-in documentation states terms, a licence or a rate limit for the data.
findings.handling: Recorded as a possible source of Tesla's data. Nothing has been requested. Under the OCPI 2.2.1 credentials handshake that the form starts, the requester supplies its own token and the address of its own OCPI versions endpoint, and must host versions and credentials endpoints that Tesla calls. The map is a static site, so on 2026-10-16 the repository owner decided to answer those calls from a separate Cloudflare Worker that only does the handshake (ADR 0025). The operator stays switched off until Tesla's terms are read.

findings.summary: Tesla's signed-in documentation says it extends OCPI 2.2.1. Locations gain access_type and evse_count fields. Tariffs gain a CONGESTION_TIME price component and min_vehicle_soc and min_congestion_threshold restrictions, none of which are in OCPI 2.2.1. The documentation also spells the connector field "tarrif_ids" (OCPI 2.2.1: tariff_ids) and describes power_type and one status field in US terms ("DCFC, AC Level 2"; "operational, under construction, planned, or decommissioned") rather than OCPI 2.2.1 values.
findings.handling: Not fetched yet, so how the data really looks needs testing. Before Tesla prices are shown, the adapter work must make sure a price that depends on these extensions is never shown as if it had no condition; how such tariffs are shown is for the repository owner to decide. Values that are not OCPI 2.2.1 values are recorded as unknown, as for every operator.
